questions.q: Which package manager and format does Ubuntu use?
options: dnf and .rpm
apt and .deb
zypper and .rpm
pacman and .pkg
questions.explain: Ubuntu is Debian-based, so it uses apt as its package manager and the .deb package format.

questions.q: What are Rocky Linux and AlmaLinux?
options: Rolling-release distributions unrelated to any enterprise distro
Free, binary-compatible community rebuilds of Red Hat Enterprise Linux
Desktop-only forks of Ubuntu
Red Hat's paid enterprise support tiers
questions.explain: Rocky Linux and AlmaLinux are free community distributions built to be binary-compatible with RHEL, filling the gap left when CentOS changed its model.

questions.q: Why do regulated enterprises often standardize on RHEL rather than a rolling-release distro?
options: RHEL has no package manager, so there's nothing to update
RHEL major versions get a full 10-year support lifecycle, meaning infrequent, plannable migrations
RHEL is the only distro that can run on physical hardware
Rolling-release distros cannot run any server software
questions.explain: RHEL's 10-year major-version lifecycle lets enterprises plan migrations roughly once a decade, versus a rolling release that changes continuously with no fixed version to certify against.

questions.q: What does "LTS" mean in the context of an Ubuntu release like 22.04?
options: Linux Terminal Shell, a type of command-line interface
Long-Term Support — a release guaranteed security updates for a fixed, multi-year window
A license fee tier for Ubuntu Server
A certification exam for Linux administrators
questions.explain: LTS releases like Ubuntu 22.04 are guaranteed updates for a fixed window (5 years standard, extendable to 10), making them the right choice for production servers.

questions.q: Which factor was NOT part of why Northbridge Retail chose Ubuntu Server 22.04 LTS?
options: No budget yet for RHEL-style paid support contracts
The team already had familiarity with apt
Strong first-class Ubuntu image support on AWS
A company-wide mandate requiring a rolling-release distro
questions.explain: Northbridge Retail's decision was driven by cost, existing team familiarity with apt, and solid AWS support for Ubuntu LTS images — not a rolling-release mandate, which is generally a poor fit for production servers.
